Question ID: STAT_U03_L02_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.2

In the model y = 6x + 10, what is the slope?

feedback.text: This is the y-intercept, not the slope.
This adds the slope and intercept, which does not identify the slope.
The variable x is the input, not the slope.
The slope is the coefficient of x, so each 1-unit increase in x changes the prediction by 6.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U03_L02_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.2

In y = 6x + 10, what does the y-intercept mean if x is hours and y is cost?

answer.text: The cost increases by 6 dollars each hour

feedback.text: That describes the slope, not the y-intercept.

answer.text: The predicted starting cost is 10 dollars when x = 0

feedback.text: The y-intercept is the predicted value when the input is 0.

answer.text: The total cost is always 6 dollars

feedback.text: The model changes with x, so cost is not always 6 dollars.
A linear model can make predictions within a reasonable range.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U03_L02_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.2

Use y = 4x + 30 to predict y when x = 5.

feedback.text: Substitute 5 for x and simplify.
This substitutes incorrectly; 4 times 5 is 20, not 4.
This adds 5 to 30 but does not multiply 4 by 5 first.
This multiplies 30 by 5 and ignores the model structure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U03_L02_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.2

Why can prediction far outside the data range be risky?

answer.text: The slope disappears outside the data range

feedback.text: The slope does not disappear, but the model may not remain appropriate.

answer.text: The y-intercept becomes the only useful value

feedback.text: The intercept does not replace the whole model.

answer.text: The relationship may not continue the same way

feedback.text: Extrapolation assumes the pattern continues beyond the observed data.
Equations can use large values, but the context may make the prediction unreliable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U03_L02_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.2

Which scatterplot pattern best supports a linear model?

answer.text: Points that cluster around a straight-line pattern

feedback.text: A linear model is appropriate when the relationship is roughly straight.
A circular pattern is not well modeled by a line.
No visible pattern does not support a useful linear model.

answer.text: Points that alternate randomly up and down

feedback.text: Random alternating points do not show a clear straight-line relationship.
